items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-19
items.q: Danny Barker's made a lot of records with me.

ctx.x: So, I called Bechet and he suggested Sidney D. Paris and Gate Mouth. And so, I just made a deal with him to bring him in. And, in fact, it was Sidney who taught me the procedure. He says, well, you send us the tickets. And as soon as we get the tickets, we'll consider that a firm commitment and we'll come in. You see. So, we set the time and I got some local musicians that I already knew from Philadelphia. And so, everything came together. And in 1936, in the beginning of 1936, we had the jazz concert where…
Did you have, in producing these concerts, did you have a stake more in the New Orleans musicians than you did in others? Or did you do?

items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-03
items.q: the first session that I made under my own aegis... was a record of Dan Burley called Chicken Shack Shuffled, 78, with, uh, Pop Sposter and Danny Barker and Jimmy Archie.

ctx.x: Well, do you remember musicians that lived in the neighborhood down there?

I remember Danny Barker, although I didn't know him at the time. But, uh, I do remember Danny performing with one of the skiffle bands in the street, and, uh, playing a cigar box and dancing and singing. You didn't see him in his home or anything like that? No.
Didn't know him socially. Yeah. I didn't know his name, for that matter.

items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-19
items.q: Danny Barker's made a lot of records with me.

ctx.x: And, uh, this is how I met people like Danny Barker, for instance. Uh-huh. Even though I had seen him performing in New Orleans when I was a kid, I didn't know his name and I didn't identify the name with the person until I met him in backstage at Nixon's Grand and Red Allen and people like that.
Did you have, in producing these concerts, did you have a stake more in the New Orleans musicians than you did in others?
